- Carries the `cutover migrate --shrink-oversized-disks` change from `mngr/deploy-retirement` (cherry-picked): its `origin_disk_gb` state-record field is what a concurrent sweep writes into the shared cutover state dir, and without it this tree's frozen record model refused to list that dir, so every new sweep or repave invocation crashed at start.

- `cutover migrate`'s health probe no longer parks a workspace for a template program its own supervisord config leaves stopped (`STOPPED   Not started`, i.e. `autostart=false`): a self-updated workspace runs a newer template than its version tag names, and the `browser` service stopped autostarting in a later release. Such a program is reported in the outcome like an owner-added one; a template program stopped by hand still blocks.

- `wireguard sync-peers` now syncs a single canary box first (the first prepped gen-2 box in the registry, or `--canary-server-id`) and re-reads its `wg0` over a fresh session; unless the interface is active with exactly the committed peers, it stops before touching any other box. A peer list the boxes reject (such as the invalid operator key that took production's `wg0` down on 2026-09-21) can now break one box, not the fleet. The per-box sync session is also bounded to two minutes instead of the prep's thirty, so a session the `wg0` restart severs is reported promptly.

- The gen-2 WireGuard prep section (run by `server prep` / `setup` and by `wireguard sync-peers`) now has `wg` parse the rendered `wg0.conf` on a scratch interface before it replaces the installed one, failing the box with the live interface untouched when `wg` refuses it, and restores the previous config if `wg-quick@wg0` still fails to restart. Either guard would have kept the 2026-09-21 invalid-key sync from taking a box's overlay down.

- Peer-only changes to a gen-2 box's `wg0.conf` are now applied live with `wg syncconf` instead of restarting `wg-quick@wg0`: the interface stays up, the operator's own session (which the sync arrives over) survives, and a fleet `sync-peers` finishes in seconds rather than tens of seconds per box. Only an `[Interface]` change (address, port, key) still restarts the interface. A failed reload restores the previous config like a failed restart does.
